```yaml
name: PR Issue Link Check

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, synchronize]

jobs:
  check-issue-link:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v2
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install regex

      - name: Validate issue links
        id: validate_issue_links
        run: |
          python .github/scripts/validate_issue_links.py
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Comment on PR if issue links are invalid
        if: steps.validate_issue_links.outputs.is_valid == 'false'
        uses: thollander/actions-comment-pull-request@e4a76dd2b0a3c2027c3fd84147a67c22ee4c90fa
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          pr-number: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          message: |
            :warning: Pull Request is not linked to any valid issue. Please link it to an existing issue using one of the following formats:
            - Fixes #123
            - Closes #456
            - Resolves #789
```

Note: This workflow assumes there is a script named `validate_issue_links.py` located at `.github/scripts/validate_issue_links.py` which contains the logic to validate issue links in pull request descriptions, titles, or commit messages. You will need to implement this script based on your specific requirements.
